what_happened: The job "Make athena drain work user-queued (ask --later) requests too" ended failed. The producer's final report was sent back with a problem still present. One acceptance criterion was unmet or not reported: the fix must be in the shared queue selection, not a special case for the named job ids, with ordering and retry rules unchanged. The event lists no blocker or major findings and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered. The report is kept in invocations/03-producer.json.
cause: Completion is judged only once, on the producer's final report. Nothing requires the producer to map each criterion to evidence before it may report done. The unmet criterion is a negative, structural one: the change must not be special-cased, and ordering and retry must not change. A passing test for the named case does not show this. The producer was never required to show where the selection change lives, or to run a test that uses ids other than the named ones, so the gap surfaced only at the end. This is the sixth case in this class.
prevention: Add a gate that blocks a producer's final report until it includes a table mapping every acceptance criterion to evidence, and rejects the report as incomplete if any criterion has no row. For structural criteria such as "not a special case", the evidence must be a named test that exercises the shared selection path with ids and request kinds other than the named ones, plus tests showing ordering and retry behavior are unchanged. The gate runs before the verifier sees the report, so gaps are returned to the producer early instead of failing the job.
proposed_request: Make athena drain pick up user-queued requests (created with `ask --later`) as well as the items it already works. Outcome: after one drain run, a queued user request is worked in the same way as any other queued item. Put the fix in the shared queue selection code, with no special case for particular job ids or for the ids seen in the failed job. Keep ordering and retry rules exactly as they are now. Before reporting done, include a table that lists each requirement and the evidence for it: the location of the selection change, a test that uses a user-queued request with an id not seen before and shows it is drained, and tests showing ordering and retry behavior are unchanged. Run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`, and record the results in the report.
